A.explanation: At zero displacement particle speed is maximum, and shifting the profile right makes this downward-sloping zero move positive, so the particle moves fastest upwards.

B.explanation: Point B is at the trough of maximum negative displacement where the transverse particle velocity is momentarily zero.

C.explanation: Point C is at zero displacement so speed is maximum, but shifting the profile right makes it move negative, so it is moving fastest downwards.

D.explanation: Point D is at the crest of maximum positive displacement where the transverse particle velocity is momentarily zero.

hints: Notice the axes show displacement against distance at one instant, with the wave profile moving to the right, and find where displacement is zero compared to the crests and troughs.
Recall that transverse particle speed is maximum at equilibrium displacement and zero at maximum displacement, so the fastest upwards motion must occur at a zero crossing.
Imagine shifting the whole sine-like profile a small distance to the right and check which sloping zero crossing goes from zero toward positive displacement, which means upward particle motion.
walkthrough: Identify the given information: a displacement-distance graph of a transverse wave moving to the right, with two zero crossings of opposite slope and a trough and a crest marked.
State the physical rule: particle speed $v$ is maximum when displacement is zero and zero when displacement is maximum, so fastest motion must be at a zero crossing, not at the trough or crest.

Use the wave-shift method: after a short time $\Delta t$ the whole profile moves a small distance $\Delta x$ to the right, so the new displacement at a fixed distance equals the old displacement just to its left.
Apply this at the downward-sloping zero: the material just to its left is positive, so this point will become positive and the particle there must be moving upwards with maximum speed.

Contrast this at the upward-sloping zero: the material just to its left is negative, so that point will become negative and the particle there moves downwards with maximum speed, while crest and trough stay near maximum with near-zero velocity.
Therefore the downward-sloping zero crossing with fastest upward particle velocity matches the marked point. This is option A
